text: Spike (SEQUENCED AFTER CD1EAE09): Spark notebook data-lineage tracking. Model DataFrame/temp-view/table read->write edges across PySpark + %%sql cells in .ipynb notebooks (spark.read/table/sql, createOrReplaceTempView, write.saveAsTable, INSERT/CREATE TABLE AS). Notebook-native alternative to function call graph. Depends on Python calls spike CD1EAE09 landing first.

DELIBERATION-SPIKE: Python module-namespace-qualified call resolution (proper fix for cross-module same-name ambiguity; open PR #277 thread python.rs:269).
Feasibility: YES. Extend engram's existing canonical-path resolution (built for Rust) to Python's module namespace. function_meta.canonical_path column already exists (cozo_queries.rs:924-940) but is Rust-only populated (empty for Python; code_graph.rs:143-160). function_ids_by_canonical_path() + reresolve_calls_edges_with_canonical_context already implement canonical-indexed resolution. Python modules ARE namespaces (foo/bar.py -> foo.bar): resolve bare call = defined-in-module -> M.name; else imported via `from N import name` -> N.name; else ambiguous/dynamic -> drop.

Scope boundary (critical): resolves MODULE-LEVEL functions and module.func() disambiguation (the same-name-different-module case). Does NOT resolve instance-method dispatch (self.method()/obj.method()) -- needs type inference; documented non-goal.

Extraction gap: python.rs:72-141 captures only a flat import_path string; needs a symbol-level import-binding table (from N import parse as p) -- the Python analogue of Rust's UseGraph.

Fail-closed (013-D no-false-edge): star imports, relative/package-root ambiguity (__init__.py, PEP 420 namespace packages), re-exports, importlib/dynamic import.

Shape: own feature (deliberation -> spike -> plan). Layers on 094-F U3 language-scoping. New work: Python import-binding capture + Python canonical_path populator + Python-aware canonical resolver. Sequence per operator ordering (after Python calls 094-F, and after Spark lineage 07BFA98E). Follow up in a later staging operation.

Related: the same-file same-name shadowing correctness bug is SPLIT OUT to stash FF7DE872 as an INDEPENDENT direct-edge/source-order fix (find_function_id first-match on the direct-edge path, code_graph.rs:896-908) -- NOT a special case this feature subsumes and NOT gated behind this deliberation. The canonical index this feature extends fails closed on duplicate canonical_path (cozo_queries.rs:1021-1025) and only disambiguates cross-file/cross-module staged calls, so it cannot fix the same-file shadowing case.

Same-file duplicate function-name shadowing produces a WRONG call edge (013-D no-false-edge / 082-F target-correctness violation). find_function_id (src/services/code_graph.rs:2037) returns the FIRST match by name, so when a file has multiple top-level defs of the same name (legal in Python; last def shadows), a bare call binds to the earlier/shadowed target instead of the effective one. Newly EXPOSED (not introduced) by Python 094-F; the shared consumer also affects Rust same-name-in-different-modules-per-file. Same-file target-precision gap ONLY -- does NOT create cross-file or cross-language false edges (094-F U3/U4 invariants hold). Fix: fail closed on >1 same-file same-name candidate (mirror the cross-file singleton post-pass ambiguity handling) OR implement source-order/last-wins semantics; add a Rust-path regression test to prove no recall regression. Split from FE8B3B2D as an INDEPENDENT direct-edge/source-order fix -- NOT resolved by FE8B3B2D and NOT gated behind the namespace-resolution deliberation. Rationale: same-file bare calls take the DIRECT-edge path (find_function_id first-match, code_graph.rs:896-908) BEFORE any canonical/singleton post-processing; only callee-unresolved cross-file calls are staged for the post-pass FE8B3B2D extends, and the canonical index fails closed on duplicate canonical_path (cozo_queries.rs:1021-1025), so the namespace feature cannot apply the source-order/last-wins semantics this bug needs. Origin: 094-F Copilot review thread on python.rs:269 (PR #277).
